products.name: The Meat Counter — What We Cut, and When
products.blurb:
Ray Sowinski has cut meat in this building for thirty-one years. Teo Barragan started in 2022 and does Sundays and Ray's days off. Between them the counter is staffed every hour the store is open, which is not true of any other grocery counter in the county.

[b]What comes in whole.[/b] Ribeyes, strip loins, whole pork loins, chucks, briskets, chickens. We break them here. Nothing in the case was cut somewhere else and put in a tray, and you can watch through the glass if you want to, because that is where the window is.

[b]Grinding.[/b] Chuck goes through at six in the morning and again about one. Round and sirloin are ground to order. The grinder is broken down and washed at close every night, which is the part of this job nobody puts on a website.

[b]Ask for it.[/b] Two inch chops. A standing rib for six. A loin butterflied. A chicken cut in eight instead of four. None of it costs extra and none of it takes long, except at four o'clock on a Saturday, when everything takes long.

[b]What we do not do.[/b] We do not take in a half beef, a hog or a deer. That is a locker's work and we are not a locker. [url=synth://tesslerlocker.synth/]Tessler Locker[/url] does it, they are twenty minutes out, and they are full from the first week of November. Call them in September like everybody who has done this before.

We do not cure or smoke anything here. The bacon and the smoked chops come from [url=synth://nyemillsdairy.synth/]Nye Mills[/url].

[b]The inspection.[/b] Routine inspection Wednesday 26 August 2026, score 96. Two violations, four points. Four pans of chicken salad in the service case had no date on them and were dated off the production log while the inspector stood there. There is a half inch gap under the receiving door on the alley side and there has been a half inch gap under that door since before the door was ours. The walk-in thermometer reads three degrees low and is tagged. Everything else was in range. Read it yourself at [url=synth://verityhealth.gov/s/inspection-results]the health department[/url] rather than asking us, because our version of it will always sound better than the inspector's.

reviews.title: The paragraph on this page is wrong
reviews.body:
The water is water. One star is for the paragraph the website put underneath it.

It was 11 June 2003, not 2004. It was not lightning. The state commission put out a two page summary in November 2003 and it says insulation degradation consistent with age, and Verity Valley has never released its own report.

Nobody died. Two Gridfall volunteers were treated at County General for smoke and went home the same afternoon.

It is all on [url=synth://wiki.gridfall.net/wiki/substation-fire-2003]the wiki[/url] with the dates on it. I asked at the register and the girl said they have tried and the box is not theirs. I believe her. I am putting it here because here is where people read it.

products.name: Our Story
products.blurb:
Amos Hollis opened a grocery at 160 Mill Street in 1913. The family has run it since. That is 113 years, four generations and the same building.

Amos had the store until 1948. His son Warren had it until 1981. Warren's son Gordon has had it since, and does the ordering at a desk in the back at five in the morning because that is when the desk is quiet. Gordon's daughter Alma runs the front end, the books and this website, and keys the ad prices in on Tuesday nights after close, which takes about ninety minutes and is the only reason the numbers on this site are right.

[b]The building.[/b] The front half is original. The back half is a 1938 addition that was a feed room before it was a stockroom. The walk-in came out of a hotel in New Ardo in 1962 and the door still says the hotel's name on the inside. The register from 1977 is on a shelf in the office and Gordon will not throw it out.

[b]March 1994.[/b] The creek came up Mill Street and got eleven inches into the store. There is a pencil line on the doorframe by the bread rack. It is not a decoration and nobody has ever painted over it. We were closed nine days.

[b]June 2003.[/b] The power went out at about ten to five in the morning and came back a little after two in the afternoon. We lost the entire frozen case and most of the dairy. The ice cream went to the fairgrounds in a truck because they had opened the exhibition hall and there were people in it.

[b]The eggs.[/b] On the last morning of the Blue Kestrel they ran out of eggs before ten and somebody came down the street for more. We sent eleven dozen and did not take the money. The Kestrel Letter wrote it up one spring and said nine dozen. It was eleven. Gordon still has the ticket he wrote it off on.

In September 2004 four retired men from the county highway department who had sat in the back booths of that diner on Tuesday mornings started sitting at the end of our deli counter instead. They are still there. There are still four of them and they are not all the same four.

[b]Mill Street.[/b] There were 22 occupied storefronts on this block in 1979 and 11 in 2007, which is the county planning office's count and not ours. Somebody wrote this year that downtown vacancy is stable. It is stable. Eleven is stable. We are the oldest thing on the street and we would rather not be the last thing on it.

reviews.title: The pencil line
reviews.body:
I have photographed that doorframe for the library's flood file, with Gordon standing next to it holding a tape.

The gauge at the Mill Street bridge crested at 14.2 feet on 8 March 1994 and the Ledger of 9 March printed it. Eleven inches in the store on this block is consistent with that and it is the only interior measurement from a business on Mill Street that anyone has written down anywhere.

products.name: Online Ordering — How This Actually Works
products.blurb:
The order form on this site sends an email to the store. That is all it does. It does not reserve anything, it does not charge anything, and there is no cart that knows what is on the shelf.

Alma reads the orders between 6:15 and 7 in the morning and again after the lunch rush. If you order at eleven at night, it is read at quarter past six.

[b]The form asks for[/b]
[list][*]Your name and a phone number that you answer[*]Pickup or Thursday delivery, and an address if delivery[*]What you want, in words, one thing per line[*]Weights for anything off the meat counter, and roughly is fine[*]Whether we should substitute or leave it out[/list]

[b]Put a real phone number in.[/b] If there is no pork loin the size you asked for, we call you. We cannot email you back, because the platform sends the order from an address that does not receive.

[b]Timing.[/b] Pickup orders in before 4 p.m. are ready the next morning. Delivery orders have to be in by 4 p.m. Wednesday or they wait a week. Meat counter items need the same two days a special cut needs, because it is the same counter and the same person.

[b]Paying.[/b] At the register, or at the truck. We do not take a card over the phone and we do not take a card at the door.

[b]The apostrophe.[/b] If you put an apostrophe in the notes box, the email arrives cut off at the apostrophe and we lose the rest of your order. We have reported this twice, in March and in July. Write [i]do not[/i] rather than the short way and it comes through whole.

If the form is being difficult, call 782-3811 and read it to whoever picks up. That worked for eighty years and it still works.

products.name: Paying, and the Things We Still Take
products.blurb:
Cash, debit, credit, EBT, WIC, and a check with a local address on it.

EBT works at the register and does not work on the Thursday truck. That is a state rule about where the card has to be present and it is not ours and we cannot get around it. If that is your situation, ring the store and ask for Alma, because there is usually something we can do about the getting-here part that is not against anybody's rules.

The tap reader on lane 1 works about four times in five. It is the reader. The processor has had it on a list since February. Lane 2's is fine.

We do not do cash back over twenty dollars, because there is one bank run a day and it goes at three.

The county's food pantry barrel is by the door and the church collects it Monday mornings. [url=synth://stmarks-verity.org/pantry]St Mark's runs it[/url] and they will tell you what they are short of, which in September is always peanut butter and always tinned tomatoes.
